body:
## Summary

`Parser.parse()` returns the same reference for a bare atom and a quoted atom, so a consumer cannot tell `1` from `'1'`. Requested: keep a `quoted` flag (or the quote character) on parsed references, without changing equality or formatting.

## Reproduction (links-notation 0.27.1, JavaScript)

```js
import { Parser } from 'links-notation';
const [link] = new Parser().parse("(t 1 '1')");
console.log(link.values.map((v) => [v.id, v.values.length]));
// [ [ 't', 0 ], [ '1', 0 ], [ '1', 0 ] ]  -- both atoms are identical
```

## Why it matters

The UI dialect of link-foundation/ui (`ui-dialect/0`, link-foundation/ui#11) has to decide how values are typed. Because the quoting is lost, the specification makes typing purely schema-driven: the declared property type decides how `16px`, `150ms` or `1` are read, and quoting never changes a type. A `quoted` flag would let a later dialect version (and lino-objects-codec) use "bare means number/boolean, quoted means string" for free-form properties without a second reader.

## Proposal

- Add an optional `quoted` property (for example `null`, `"'"`, `'"'` or `` '`' ``) to references produced by `parse()` and `parseGroups()`.
- Keep `equals()` and `format()` unchanged by default, so existing users see no difference.
- Mirror the flag in the other language ports so that conformance fixtures can rely on it.

title: Parsed references lose whether they were quoted: (t 1 '1') gives two equal references
